native_retrieval.title: RSS - Wikipedia
native_retrieval.snippet: # RSS. For RSS feeds from Wikipedia, see Wikipedia:Syndication. | Type of format | Web syndication |. **RSS** (**RDF Site Summary**, **Rich Site Summary** or **Really Simple Syndication**) is a web feed that allows users and applications to access updates to websites in a standardized, computer-readable format. Although RSS formats have evolved from as early as March 1999, it was between 2005 and 2006 when RSS gained widespread use, and the ("") icon was decided upon by several major web browsers. RSS feed data is presented to users using software called a news aggregator and the passing of content is called web syndication. Users subscribe to feeds either by entering a feed's URI into the reader or by clicking on the browser's feed icon. In July 1999, Dan Libby of Netscape produced a new version, RSS 0.91, which simplified the format by removing RDF elements and incorporating elements from Dave Winer's news syndication format.

The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) is a Hindu nationalist volunteer organization founded in 1925 in colonial India by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar. The BJP is a political party that was established in 1980 and has its origins in the Bharatiya Jana Sangh (BJS), which was founded in 1951 as the political wing of the RSS. It was founded in 1925 by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar (1889–1940), a physician from the Maharashtra region of India, as a cultural organization to promote discipline, unity, and a sense of identity among Hindus at a time of communal tensions in colonial India.

native_retrieval.snippet: # The Early History of the RSS: A Reading List. Read EPW's editorial on the topic [**here**]. 1) In this article written in 1972, the first of a four-part historical narrative of the origins and growth of the RSS, the author deals with the disenchantment of many Congressmen with Gandhi's Non-Co-operation Movement and with efforts at Hindu-Muslim togetherness. This attracts the attention of the Government of India which begins to keep a close watch on it In order to prepare for the post-War period and the expected Hindu-Muslim troubles, the RSS decides at the beginning of the Second World War not to antagonise the Government in any way. In 1937 Savarkar was elected President of the Mahasabha and settled these differences by resolving to build it into a political organisation representing the Hindus. And the RSS did not want to be associated with a group which would have placed it in direct opposition to the Congress. Upto the time of the ban, many swayamsevaks were members of the Congress.
